title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel

code.title: hojonathanho/diffusion
code.note: the authors' TensorFlow code (repo, about 15 minutes for the README and entry path); GitHub shows no licence file

run_label: sample from four trained toy DDPMs
takeaway: Reparameterising the diffusion ELBO as noise prediction (L_simple, epsilon-MSE) made diffusion models generate SOTA images (CIFAR-10 FID 3.17) and founded the modern diffusion era.
verdict: Believe the recipe: it was reproduced independently within a year (FID 3.29 against 3.17) and every diffusion model since descends from it. Read the 3.17 itself as one training run whose checkpoint was chosen by the same FID, against a GAN baseline that later beat it, and take the paper at its word that its likelihoods are not competitive.

headline.d: best unconditional FID in Table 1 (lower is better); Inception Score 9.46

an interactive walk through Stable Diffusion's denoising loop on real prompts: the latent-space descendant of this paper, step by step.

kb.n: 2021-12: runs this exact DDPM machinery in a compressed VAE latent space, making high-resolution text-to-image tractable.
2021-02: supplies the text conditioning that later diffusion systems bolt onto the DDPM backbone (DALL-E 2 samples from CLIP latents).
2020-10: the DiT line replaces DDPM's U-Net with this Transformer architecture, on latent patches.
2017: the sinusoidal position embedding DDPM uses to tell its network the timestep t.
2026: diffusion applied to text generation, where the recipe's denoise-in-parallel idea meets language models.

topics.n: diffusion and flow models in context.
the ELBO, KL divergence between Gaussians and score matching that the derivation rests on.
